Ten Principles of Economics: Scarcity
The limited nature of society's resources
Opportunity cost
What must be given up to obtain something
Rational actor
A decision maker who systematically does the best they can
Marginal change
A small incremental adjustment to a plan of action
Incentive
Something inducing a person to act
Gains from trade
The mutual benefit when parties specialise and exchange
Market economy
An economy allocating resources through decentralised decisions
Invisible hand
Smith's idea that self-interest can produce socially good outcomes
Property rights
The ability to own and control a scarce resource
Efficiency versus equity
Maximising total benefit versus distributing it fairly
Thinking Like an Economist: A descriptive claim about how the world is
A prescriptive claim about how the world ought to be
A graph showing the maximum combinations producible
The study of individual households and firms
The ability to produce at a lower opportunity cost
The ability to produce more with the same inputs
A model of money and goods moving between households and firms
A simplified representation used to understand real behaviour
Supply and Demand: Quantity demanded falls as price rises
A table relating price to quantity demanded
Movement along the demand curve caused by a price change
A shift of the entire curve caused by a non-price factor
A good whose demand rises as income rises
A good whose demand falls as income rises
Goods used in place of each other
Quantity supplied rises as price rises
The price where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded
Excess quantity supplied at a price above equilibrium
Excess quantity demanded at a price below equilibrium
Elasticity: Price elasticity of demand
The responsiveness of quantity demanded to a price change
Elastic demand
Elasticity greater than one, where quantity responds strongly
Inelastic demand
Elasticity less than one, where quantity barely responds
Unit elastic
Elasticity of exactly one, where revenue does not change with price
Determinants of elasticity
Substitutes, necessity, time horizon, and share of income
Total revenue test
Raising price increases revenue only when demand is inelastic
Income elasticity of demand
How demand responds to a change in income
Cross-price elasticity
How demand for one good responds to another good's price
Price elasticity of supply
How responsive quantity supplied is to price
Perfectly inelastic demand
A vertical curve where quantity never changes with price
Consumer Surplus and Efficiency: Willingness to pay
The maximum a buyer would pay for a good
Consumer surplus
Willingness to pay minus the price actually paid
Producer surplus
Price received minus the seller's cost
Total surplus
Consumer plus producer surplus, a measure of market gain
Allocative efficiency
Resources allocated so total surplus is maximised
Market efficiency
The outcome where no reallocation could make someone better off without harming another
Cost to a seller
The value of everything a seller gives up to produce
Efficient market outcome
Goods going to the buyers who value them most
Welfare economics
The study of how resource allocation affects wellbeing
Market failure
A situation where free markets fail to allocate efficiently
Taxes and Deadweight Loss: Tax incidence
Who actually bears the burden of a tax
Tax wedge
The gap a tax creates between what buyers pay and sellers receive
Deadweight loss
The lost surplus from transactions a tax prevents
Elasticity and tax burden
The more inelastic side of the market bears more of the tax
Price ceiling
A legal maximum price, producing shortages when binding
Price floor
A legal minimum price, producing surpluses when binding
Binding constraint
A price control set on the restrictive side of equilibrium
Subsidy
A government payment that lowers effective price and raises quantity
Laffer curve
The idea that beyond some rate, higher taxes reduce revenue
Lump-sum tax
A fixed tax that does not distort behaviour at the margin
Externalities and Public Goods: A cost or benefit falling on a third party
A spillover cost such as pollution
A spillover benefit such as education
Making decision makers face the full social cost
A tax set to correct a negative externality
Private bargaining can solve externalities when transaction costs are low
A market-based mechanism for allocating emissions rights
A good that is non-rival and non-excludable
Benefiting from a good without paying for it
A rival but non-excludable good prone to overuse
Depletion of a shared resource through individual self-interest
Costs of Production: A direct monetary payment for an input
An opportunity cost requiring no monetary outlay
Revenue minus both explicit and implicit costs
A cost that does not vary with output
A cost that rises with output
The additional cost of producing one more unit
Total cost divided by quantity produced
Each additional input unit adding less output than the last
Average cost falling as output expands
Average cost rising as output expands beyond an efficient size
The output level minimising average total cost
A cost already incurred and irrelevant to future decisions
Perfect Competition: Perfectly competitive market
Many buyers and sellers of an identical product with free entry
Price taker
A firm that must accept the prevailing market price
Marginal revenue
The additional revenue from selling one more unit
Profit maximisation rule
Produce where marginal revenue equals marginal cost
Shutdown decision
Stop producing in the short run when price falls below average variable cost
Exit decision
Leave the industry long run when price is below average total cost
Short-run supply curve
The marginal cost curve above average variable cost
Long-run equilibrium
Zero economic profit with price equal to minimum average total cost
Free entry and exit
The mechanism driving long-run profit toward zero
Constant cost industry
An industry whose long-run supply curve is horizontal
Monopoly: Monopoly
A single seller facing the entire market demand curve
Barrier to entry
An obstacle preventing competitors from entering
Natural monopoly
An industry where one firm can supply at lowest total cost
Market power
The ability to influence the market price
Marginal revenue under monopoly
Below price, because selling more requires cutting price on all units
Monopoly output rule
Produce where marginal revenue equals marginal cost, then charge what demand allows
Deadweight loss of monopoly
Lost surplus from restricting output below the efficient level
Price discrimination
Charging different buyers different prices for the same good
Perfect price discrimination
Charging each buyer exactly their willingness to pay
Antitrust law
Legislation limiting anticompetitive conduct and market concentration
Regulation of natural monopoly
Setting price near marginal or average cost
Monopolistic Competition: Monopolistic competition
Many firms selling differentiated products with free entry
Product differentiation
Making a product distinct from close substitutes
Excess capacity
Producing below efficient scale, a feature of this market structure
Markup over marginal cost
Price exceeding marginal cost, unlike perfect competition
Advertising
Spending intended to shift demand and build brand loyalty
Brand name
A signal of consistent quality that also creates market power
Long-run zero profit
Entry eroding profit until price equals average total cost
Downward-sloping firm demand
Each firm's own demand curve slopes down due to differentiation
Comparison to monopoly
Similar markup but no long-run profit due to free entry
Comparison to perfect competition
Differentiated products and excess capacity rather than efficient scale
Oligopoly and Game Theory: Oligopoly
A market dominated by a few interdependent firms
Strategic interaction
Each firm's best move depending on what rivals do
Collusion
An agreement among firms to restrict output and raise price
Cartel
A formal collusive arrangement acting like a joint monopoly
Game theory
The study of strategic decision making among interdependent actors
Dominant strategy
A choice best regardless of what others do
Nash equilibrium
An outcome where no player benefits from changing strategy alone
Prisoner's dilemma
A game where individually rational choices produce a worse joint outcome
Tit-for-tat
A repeated-game strategy of mirroring the opponent's last move
Price war
Competitive undercutting that erodes profits across an industry
Concentration ratio
The share of market held by the largest firms
Labor Markets: Derived demand
Demand for an input driven by demand for the output it produces
Marginal product of labour
The extra output from one more worker
Value of the marginal product
Marginal product multiplied by the output price
Labour demand curve
The value of marginal product curve for a competitive firm
Labour supply
The trade-off workers make between labour and leisure
Equilibrium wage
The wage where labour supplied equals labour demanded
Human capital
The knowledge and skills embodied in workers
Compensating differential
Extra pay offsetting undesirable job characteristics
Monopsony
A market with a single buyer, which suppresses wages
Labour union
A worker organisation bargaining collectively over pay and conditions
Efficiency wages
Paying above market rate to raise productivity and retention
Income Inequality and Poverty: Asymmetric information
One party to a transaction knowing more than the other
Adverse selection
Hidden characteristics driving good participants out of a market
Moral hazard
Hidden behaviour changing after an agreement is made
Signalling
Taking a costly action to credibly convey private information
Screening
An uninformed party acting to induce revelation of information
Principal-agent problem
Conflict when an agent's incentives diverge from the principal's
Poverty line
The income threshold defining official poverty
Gini coefficient
A single number summarising income inequality
In-kind transfer
Assistance delivered as goods or services rather than cash
Negative income tax
A system paying households below a certain income level
Progressive taxation
Higher earners paying a larger share of income in tax
